Can microbes make milk and egg proteins as cheaply as cows and hens?

Precision fermentation puts the gene for one animal protein into a yeast or a fungus. The microbes grow on sugar in large steel tanks and release the protein. The protein is then purified and dried to a powder. This model estimates what that costs for seven proteins. It compares each cost with the price of the same protein from animals.

These are estimates from an open model built on public data. No human expert has reviewed it yet. They are not any company's real costs, and not investment or business advice. About this page.

Each protein against its animal version

How many times the animal price each protein costs to make. Left of the line, fermentation is cheaper. Click a protein to see how its cost builds up.

Accounting (advanced)

What would make it cheaper?

The most important number is how much protein each litre of broth holds when the tank is emptied. More protein per litre means fewer tanks, a smaller plant and a lower cost. Each cell below is one model run. Click a cell to select it.

Where the money goes

Every cost is an amount per kg of protein times a unit price.

How sure is this?

Does the model get known things right?

No company publishes what its fermentation protein costs to make. So the model was tested on cases with a known answer before it was used here. A reality check compares it with a market price or a real plant. A consistency check compares it with another model. Agreeing with another model is not proof that either is right. No input was tuned to pass these tests.

About this page

Status. No human expert has reviewed this analysis yet. The author built the model, its evidence base and this page with an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic). Independent AI reviewers then audited each version, and each finding had to rest on a computation, a quote or a line of code. docs/AUDIT.md and docs/REVIEW.md in the repository log every finding and fix.

What the numbers are. Every number is a model result or exact arithmetic on one. The model costs a plant from published designs and public prices. It is not the cost of any real company or plant: no precision-fermentation company publishes one. Figures labelled “company claim” are what companies say, not measurements. The best case is a ceiling, not a forecast.

Not advice. This page is for research and discussion. It is not investment, business, regulatory or safety advice.
